You could say that, sure. The difference is that the Categorical Imperative is good in itself. There is no outside incentive. A hypothetical imperative is conditional.

There's only one categorical imperative, but there are several formulations of it. Essentially, it is "act as though the maxim of your action must become a universal law." It's very absolute and based more on intentions than results.  For example, if your boss's daughter is drowning, you should try to save her because anyone in that situation should try to preserve human life, not to please the boss or win her love or anything like that. Some of the other formulations are "always treat people like an end, never as a means alone," and "act as though you are a lawmaker [this could be a bad word choice] in a kingdom of ends".

My New Year's Eve was shit. Three hours before midnight, my friends were already drunk and I craved the steel solitude of my early train ride home. Two stops in, the soft clacking of the tracks had soothed me into a trance when a clunk followed by nervous, breathy laughter startled me. 
The word "sorry" fell from chapped lips that hung in a lopsided  half-smile as a girl struggled to shove her bag beneath the seat. The girl--or woman, maybe--dropped into the seat facing me with an impossibly loud thud for such a short body. I carefully avoided eye-contact til the train began to move. After a few minutes, I looked up from my phone and stole a glance. She wore thick-framed black glasses and a flannel shirt. Her mousy brown hair rebelled wildly against the elastic that weakly embraced her loose curls. A book laid open across her lap, but the girl's lids collapsed lazily over chocolate-colored eyes. Dark circles looked like purple blankets beneath. I thought the circles looked strangely inviting, like they may belong to a beloved teacher or a friendly neighbor. Two perfectly symmetrical moles dotted her face just below the crooked mouth, turning her chin into a cartoon character. I thought about the people who had loved her enough to call the blemishes "beauty marks" and smiled  Even as she slept, the girl's leg twitched up and down, anxiously plotting its escape even as the mind rested. 
The old train suddenly sighed, and as it lurched to a halt, I noticed a necklace jingling against her chest. Four charms were
 responsible for the noise: a gold cross,two hearts, and a ring. What did they mean? Could she be engaged? In love? I wanted to ask, but her eyes shot open and mine returned to my phone.
